question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. parliment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "parliment" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "parliament", meaning the supreme law-making body of a country. (संसद)

◦ Correct: The bill was passed by the parliament.

• Spelling key: PAR + LIA + MENT (note the silent "a" after "li").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "perceive" (to become aware of / notice), "pastime" (a hobby / leisure activity) and "perseverance" (persistence / steady effort) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words with the tricky "-iament/-ie-" pattern: parliament, friend, believe. Remember the rule "i before e except after c" (perceive, receive, deceive).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The dancer / performed weird / but the music was / highly enchanting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. performed weird.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Performed" is a verb, and a verb must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Weird" is an adjective; the adverb form "weirdly" is required. So it should be "performed weirdly".

◦ Correct: The dancer performed weirdly but the music was highly enchanting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "The dancer" (subject), "but the music was" (conjunction + subject + verb) and "highly enchanting" (adverb + adjective) are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Adjectives describe nouns (a weird dance); adverbs describe verbs, adjectives or other adverbs (danced weirdly). Most adverbs are formed by adding "-ly" to the adjective.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays the crucial role in neural communication.
option_2: An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
option_3: The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
option_4: The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft plays the crucial role in neural communication.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "dance" is a specific, particular one (defined by the "of" phrase), so it needs the definite article "the" — "The intricate dance". Similarly, "the synaptic cleft" refers to a specific, known structure.

• "plays a crucial role" is the fixed collocation — a role is being introduced generally, so the indefinite article "a" is correct.

◦ Correct: The intricate dance ... in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 4 wrongly say "plays the crucial role" (should be "a crucial role").

• Options 1 and 2 wrongly begin with "An" instead of "The".

NOTE

• Use "the" for a specific/known noun and "a/an" for a non-specific one. The idiom is "play a role / part in something".

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: If you want to have a sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.
option_2: If you want to have an sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.
option_3: If you want to have sound working knowledge of the Japanese, you must read this book.
option_4: If you want to have a sound working knowledge of the Japanese, you must read this book.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. If you want to have a sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "knowledge" is a singular countable phrase here ("a ... knowledge"), so it takes "a" (not "an", because "sound" begins with a consonant sound).

• When "Japanese" refers to the language, no article "the" is used before it — "knowledge of Japanese" (the language), not "of the Japanese".

◦ Correct: ... a sound working knowledge of Japanese ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 wrongly uses "an sound" (should be "a", since "sound" starts with a consonant sound).

• Options 3 and 4 wrongly add "the" before "Japanese" — "the Japanese" would mean the Japanese people, not the language.

NOTE

• Names of languages take no article: "I learn French", "a knowledge of Hindi". "The + language-name + people" (the Japanese) refers to the nation/people.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

RK Laxman was well-known for his drawings of people in such a highly exaggerated manner as to cause laughter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. caricatures.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "caricature" is a drawing of a person in which certain features are exaggerated in a comic or grotesque way to cause laughter. This exactly matches "drawings ... in a highly exaggerated manner as to cause laughter". (व्यंग्य-चित्र / कार्टून)

◦ Example: The cartoonist drew a hilarious caricature of the minister.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "articles" (written pieces), Option 2 "sketches" (rough drawings) and Option 3 "portraits" (realistic likenesses) do not carry the sense of comic exaggeration.

NOTE

• RK Laxman was India's most famous cartoonist, creator of "The Common Man" and the daily "You Said It" cartoon in The Times of India.

question: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
option_1: The audience applauded the muzicians performance.
option_2: The audiance applauded the musicans performance.
option_3: The audience applauded the musician's performance.
option_4: The audiance applauded the musician's perfomance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The audience applauded the musician's performance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt words are "audience", "musician's" (with the apostrophe showing possession) and "performance".

◦ Correct: The audience applauded the musician's performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "musicians" as "muzicians"; Option 2 misspells "audience" as "audiance" and drops the apostrophe; Option 4 misspells "audience" and "performance" ("audiance", "perfomance").

NOTE

• "Audience" ends in "-ience"; "performance" keeps the "r" — per-FOR-mance. The possessive of a singular noun adds 's (musician → musician's).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of 'clarify' in the sentence given below.

The last question of the examination paper confused me when it asked to illustrate the Pythagoras' theorem with the help of examples.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Illustrate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Clarify" means to make something clear or easier to understand. In the sentence, "illustrate" (to explain/make clear by giving examples) is the closest synonym. (स्पष्ट करना / उदाहरण देकर समझाना)

◦ Example: The teacher illustrated / clarified the rule with examples.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Last", Option 3 "Help" and Option 4 "Confused" do not mean "to make clear".

• "Confused" is in fact the opposite of clarify in this context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of clarify: illustrate, explain, elucidate, simplify, clear up. Antonyms: confuse, obscure, complicate.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Sarvana failed in the examination last week and is in extreme depression these days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. In the doldrums.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in the doldrums" means in a state of low spirits, depression or inactivity; feeling sad and without energy. It fits "in extreme depression". (उदास / निराश अवस्था में)

◦ Example: After losing his job, he was in the doldrums for months.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in the red" (in debt / making a loss), Option 2 "in cold blood" (cruelly and deliberately) and Option 4 "in the lurch" (abandoned in a difficult situation) do not mean depressed.

NOTE

• "Doldrums" originally referred to the equatorial ocean belt of calm, windless weather where sailing ships got stuck — hence "stuck / low / dull".

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

Shylock, the Jewish moneylender, and Antonio, the rich Merchant of Venice loathed each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. abhorred.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Loathed" means hated or detested intensely. Its closest synonym is "abhorred" (to hate/regard with disgust). (घृणा करना)

◦ Example: They loathed / abhorred each other's company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "admired" is an antonym (to respect / like).

• Option 1 "lathered" (to cover with soap foam) and Option 4 "latte" (a coffee drink) are unrelated distractors.

NOTE

• Synonyms of loathe: abhor, detest, despise, hate. Antonyms: love, adore, admire, cherish. (Shylock and Antonio are characters from Shakespeare's "The Merchant of Venice".)

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Head in the clouds
option_4: Thinking about the sky and clouds
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Being impractical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(to have one's) head in the clouds" means being impractical, day-dreaming, out of touch with reality. (अव्यावहारिक होना / कल्पनाओं में खोया रहना)

◦ Example: He will never finish the project — he always has his head in the clouds.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are literal or unrelated meanings and do not capture the figurative sense of being unrealistic/absent-minded.

NOTE

• The opposite idiom is "to have one's feet on the ground" — meaning to be practical and realistic.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Jurisdiction
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Governance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jurisdiction" means the official power or authority to make legal decisions and govern; the range of such authority. Its closest synonym here is "governance" (the act of governing / exercising authority). (अधिकार-क्षेत्र / शासन)

◦ Example: The case falls within the jurisdiction / governance of the High Court.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Expression", Option 3 "Violation" (breaking a rule) and Option 4 "Descent" (going down / ancestry) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of jurisdiction: authority, control, dominion, command, power, sway.

question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class.
option_1: Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.
option_2: Sushma is the smart girl of the class.
option_3: Sushma is smarter than any other girls in the class.
option_4: No other girl is as smart as Sushma.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "One of the smartest girls" is a superlative structure meaning she is among the top few (not the single best). Its correct positive degree form uses "Few ... as ... as ...": "Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma."

◦ Superlative: Sushma is one of the smartest girls → Positive: Few girls are as smart as Sushma.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "No other girl is as smart as Sushma" is the positive form of "Sushma is the smartest" (the single best) — a different meaning.

• Option 3 uses "than", which makes it comparative, and has a grammatical error ("any other girls").

NOTE

• Degree change of "one of the tallest": Superlative → one of the tallest; Comparative → taller than many other; Positive → very few are as tall as.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb.

Bindu asked Arya to fill out for / her so that she could / take care of / her sick father.
option_1: Bindu asked Arya to fill out for
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Bindu asked Arya to fill out for.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The intended meaning is that Arya should substitute/stand in for Bindu. The correct phrasal verb is "fill in for (someone)" = to take someone's place temporarily. "fill out" means to complete a form and is wrong here.

◦ Correct: Bindu asked Arya to fill in for her so that she could take care of her sick father.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "so that she could", "take care of" and "her sick father" are correct.

NOTE

• "Fill in for" = to substitute for someone. "Fill out / fill in" = to complete a form. "Fill up" = to make something full.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The restaurant's menu featured a variety of __________ dishes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. delicious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "delicious", meaning highly pleasing to taste; very tasty. (स्वादिष्ट)

◦ Correct: The restaurant's menu featured a variety of delicious dishes.

• Spelling key: DE + LI + CIOUS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspellings: "delecious", "delicius" and "delitious" are all incorrect.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-cious": delicious, precious, gracious, spacious, suspicious. The sound is "-shus" but spelt "-cious".

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Choose the correct alternative.

She is late than we expected.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. later.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of "late" is "later" (late – later – latest). So it should be "later than we expected".

◦ Correct: She is later than we expected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "latter" means "the second of two things" (not a comparative of time).

• Option 2 "more late" is wrong — short adjectives take "-er", never "more".

• Option 4 "latest" is the superlative and cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• "Later" (comparative of late — time) vs "latter" (the second of two). "Latest" = most recent; "last" = final.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I always prefer a small, cosy cottage ______ a high-rise apartment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "prefer" takes the preposition "to" when comparing two things: "prefer X to Y". So it should be "prefer a cottage to a high-rise apartment".

◦ Correct: I always prefer a small, cosy cottage to a high-rise apartment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "prefer ... than" is a common error; the correct form is "prefer ... to".

• When followed by verbs, we say "prefer walking to driving" or "prefer to walk rather than drive".

NOTE

• Fixed patterns: prefer A to B, superior/inferior to, senior/junior to, prior to — all take "to", never "than".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

Success demands hard work, diligence and perseverance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Effort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diligence" means careful, persistent hard work and steady application/effort. Its closest synonym is "effort" (an earnest attempt / hard work). (परिश्रम / लगन)

◦ Example: With great diligence / effort, she completed the task on time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "indolence" (laziness) is an antonym of diligence.

• Option 2 "Coolness" and Option 3 "Trouble" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of diligence: effort, industriousness, application, assiduity, perseverance. Antonyms: laziness, indolence, negligence.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who travels from place to place, especially for work
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Itinerant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "itinerant" is a person who travels from place to place, especially for work (e.g., an itinerant trader or preacher). This exactly matches the definition. (यायावर / घुमंतू कामगार)

◦ Example: The itinerant salesman moved from town to town.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Vagrant" (a homeless wanderer with no settled home or work), Option 2 "Nomad" (a member of a community that moves with its herds/seasons) and Option 3 "Pilgrim" (one who travels to a holy place) do not specifically mean travelling "for work".

NOTE

• Related words: nomad (wandering tribe), vagabond/vagrant (aimless wanderer), pilgrim (religious traveller), itinerant (travels for work).

question:
Choose the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank meaningfully.

His _______________ is a brilliant student.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. son.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a word meaning a male child, which is "son". It fits "His son is a brilliant student." (पुत्र / बेटा)

◦ Correct: His son is a brilliant student.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "sun" is a homophone but means the star at the centre of the solar system — wrong meaning here.

• Options 1 "sune" and 4 "sone" are not valid English words.

NOTE

• Homophones: "son" (male child) vs "sun" (the star). Both sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Woodcutting involves the removal of useless trees first, ________ by medium and finest quality timber trees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. followed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "followed by" means coming after in sequence. Useless trees are removed first, "followed by" medium and finest quality trees — showing the order. (उसके बाद)

◦ Correct: ... removal of useless trees first, followed by medium and finest quality timber trees.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "adjusted by", Option 3 "enacted by" and Option 4 "compared by" do not fit the idea of sequence/order.

NOTE

• "Followed by" is used to show what comes next in a series, e.g., the starter, followed by the main course, followed by dessert.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. behind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous quotation by P. B. Shelley is "If winter comes, can spring be far behind?" — meaning after hard times, good times surely follow. The fixed word is "behind". (यदि सर्दी आई है, तो वसंत दूर नहीं)

◦ Correct: "If winter comes, can spring be far behind?"

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "far" is already present in the sentence ("far ___"), so options adding another "far" (Option 3 "far behind") or extra words ("behind and far", "behind and below") make the phrase redundant or ungrammatical.

NOTE

• This line is the closing line of Shelley's poem "Ode to the West Wind", a message of hope and optimism.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. last.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Last" here is a verb meaning to continue for a period of time. The winter "will not last till perpetuity" means it will not continue forever. (बना रहना / टिकना)

◦ Correct: ... we know that it will not last till perpetuity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hold" and Option 3 "hold on" do not fit the sense of "continue for a duration" with "till perpetuity".

• Option 4 "rest" means to relax, which is illogical here.

NOTE

• "Last" as a verb = to endure/continue (The meeting lasted two hours). "Perpetuity" = a state that lasts forever.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. infuses.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Spring" is singular third person, so the verb must take "-s": "Spring infuses a new life in us." "Infuse" means to fill/instil (someone) with a quality or feeling. (भर देना / संचारित करना)

◦ Correct: Spring infuses a new life in us.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "imbue", 2 "immerse" and 3 "inculcate" are all in the base form and do not agree with the singular subject "Spring" (they would need "infuses"-type "-s"). Only "infuses" has correct subject–verb agreement.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: a singular subject (Spring) takes a singular verb with "-s" (infuses). Synonyms of infuse: instil, imbue, fill, inspire.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. come out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "come out" means to appear / emerge / bloom. Buds "come out as flowers" means the buds open and appear as flowers in spring. (खिलना / निकलना)

◦ Correct: ... buds come out as flowers ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "take out" (to remove), Option 3 "fall over" (to topple) and Option 4 "pull out" (to withdraw) do not fit the blooming of buds.

NOTE

• "Come out" has several meanings: to appear (the sun came out), to be published (the book came out), to bloom (flowers come out).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We are familiar with the quote, "If winter comes, can spring be far ___1___?" Winters are depressing, but we bear because we know that it will not ___2___ till perpetuity. Spring ___3___ a new life in us. As the spring begins to set itself, the nights become shorter and the days get longer. Gardens and lawns become colourful, buds ___4___ as flowers, birds chirp and butterflies fly from one flower to another to ___5___ on the sweet nectar. The dullness is taken over by brightness.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. suck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Butterflies feed by sucking the sweet nectar from flowers through their long tube-like tongue (proboscis). "suck on the sweet nectar" is the natural expression. (चूसना)

◦ Correct: ... butterflies fly from one flower to another to suck on the sweet nectar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gulp" (to swallow quickly), Option 3 "gobble" (to eat hurriedly, of solid food) and Option 2 "food" (a noun, not a verb) do not correctly describe how butterflies take in liquid nectar.

NOTE

• A butterfly draws up nectar with its proboscis — a coiled, straw-like mouthpart — so "suck" is the apt verb. "Suck on" = to draw liquid by suction.
